subsystems.name: Light-emitting protein system
subsystems.role: produces visible light inside skin cells.
parts: or fluorescent protein such as GFP, which needs external light to glow

subsystems.name: Gene delivery and editing
subsystems.role: inserts the light-producing genes into skin cells stably.

subsystems.name: Target skin tissue
subsystems.role: the living layer that must survive and keep expressing the genes.

subsystems.name: Substrate supply
subsystems.role: delivers luciferin and energy (ATP) to the engineered cells.

subsystems.name: Patterning and control
subsystems.role: creates shapes and allows the glow to be switched on or off.

subsystems.name: Safety and immune management
subsystems.role: prevents rejection, inflammation or cancer from edited cells.

buildSteps.title: Choose the light chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Decide between fluorescence, which needs an external lamp or UV source, and true bioluminescence, which needs a luciferase enzyme plus a luciferin fuel.

buildSteps.title: Design the genetic construct
buildSteps.detail: Codon-optimize the chosen gene, attach a promoter that works in skin cells, and add control elements so expression can be regulated.

buildSteps.title: Test in cultured skin cells
buildSteps.detail: Introduce the construct into keratinocytes or fibroblasts in the lab and measure light output, cell health and stability over many divisions.

buildSteps.title: Engineer a skin graft or in vivo delivery
buildSteps.detail: Grow sheets of modified cells for grafting, or use viral or non-viral vectors to edit skin cells directly in place.

buildSteps.title: Apply to the skin
buildSteps.detail: Place the engineered graft or inject the delivery vehicle into the dermis or epidermis, targeting the basal layer for long-term persistence.

buildSteps.title: Form the pattern
buildSteps.detail: Use localized delivery, patterned promoters or masks to create defined glowing shapes rather than uniform emission.

buildSteps.title: Supply the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Apply luciferin topically or systemically so it reaches the engineered cells; without it, true bioluminescence cannot occur.

buildSteps.title: Run safety and immune tests
buildSteps.detail: Check for immune rejection, off-target edits, tumour formation and substrate toxicity before any human use.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Track expression over time, refresh substrate as needed, and have a way to switch the system off if problems arise.

prerequisites.tech: Gene editing of human skin cells
prerequisites.why: CRISPR works in many cell types, but stable editing of skin stem cells without side effects is not yet routine.
GFP from jellyfish and luciferase enzymes from fireflies and other organisms are well studied in the lab.
lab-grown skin grafts are used clinically, but not yet carrying engineered light-producing genes.
the body may attack cells expressing foreign proteins, especially if viral vectors are used.
luciferin must reach the right cells at useful concentrations without causing toxicity or being cleared too quickly.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of light-emitting skin cells in culture
pathway.unlocks: proof that the genetic and biochemical parts can work together.

pathway.milestone: animal models showing stable, controllable glow in living skin
pathway.unlocks: evidence on longevity, immune response and substrate supply.

pathway.milestone: early human safety trials for small engineered skin patches
pathway.unlocks: data on safety and reversibility, possibly first for medical monitoring rather than art.
